title: Within one Currier language the scribe adds little: the same-scribe vocabulary effect is mostly the A/B dialect, measured on far-apart page pairs
statement: A stratified check on P-G-009 before it is registered, public pages only (practice training and evaluation together, ZL, certain paragraph words, 199 pages with at least 40), median cosine of raw word counts over page pairs. To keep local drift out, only pairs more than 15 pages apart in manuscript order are compared. Same Currier language, same section: same hand 0.268 (3,678 pairs) against different hand 0.237 (241), a difference of +0.031. Same language, different section: same hand 0.274 (2,210) against different hand 0.317 (1,787), a difference of -0.043. Different language, different section, different hand: 0.158 (6,885). So almost all of the same-scribe effect over far pages is the A/B split: pages of one language resemble each other at about 0.24 to 0.32 whoever wrote them, pages of different languages at about 0.15, and inside a language the hand moves the median by a few hundredths in either direction. Two consequences for the fact. (1) It is still a fair generator target, and the reason the drifting chain fails it stands: pages of one dialect recur far apart (herbal B among herbal A, biological and star pages), so local drift cannot carry it. A procedure with two tables used by gathering or by sheet would pass, which says the text has two dialects that alternate in the book, not that it means anything. (2) Since the hand label nearly coincides with Currier's language, and Currier's language was itself defined from the text, the scribe statistic is close to circular as evidence about scribes; registering it with the language label instead would say the same thing more plainly and with more pages, and a scribe claim needs a test inside one language. The section half of this check also confirms P-G-008: same-section, different-language far pairs (0.147) are no closer than different-section ones (0.158). Scripts were local; nothing here is scored.
check: Rerun on public pages: median page-pair cosine for pairs more than 15 pages apart, split by same or different Currier language, section and hand; a scribe fact should hold within one language before it is registered as one.
